properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 31 at 5:44PM MDT until November 2 at 9:10PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Colorado...

...This is a PARTICULARY DANGEROUS SITUATION...

For the San Juan River at Pagosa Springs affecting Archuleta County.

.Significant and historic flooding is possible along the San Juan
River at Pagosa Springs. Widespread rainfall is expected to begin
early Sunday morning and continue through Monday morning. Excessive
runoff will also increase flooding risks. The region should prepare
for a dangerous and impactful flood event.

For the San Juan River...including Pagosa Springs...major flooding is
forecast. This is a particularly dangerous situation.

* WHAT...Major flooding caused by excessive rainfall is forecast
along the San Juan River. This is a Particularly Dangerous
Situation.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Pagosa Springs.

* WHEN...From Sunday afternoon to Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Portions of San Juan Street are beginning
to flood.  Waters have reached the foundation of the Colorado
Ranger Building.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:00 PM MDT Saturday the stage was 6.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
tomorrow afternoon to a crest of 17.0 feet early Monday morning.
It will then fall below flood stage Monday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 10/05/1911.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Heed any evacuation orders from local authorities.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/gjt.

The next statement will be issued Monday evening at 915 PM MST.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 31 at 2:19PM HST until October 31 at 5:45PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
FFWHFO

The National Weather Service in Honolulu has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The island of Kauai in Kauai County

* Until 545 PM HST.

* At 219 PM HST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling over the eastern slopes of Kauai with additional
showers moving in from the southwest. Rain was falling at a rate of
up to 1 to 2 inches per hour. In addition to the Hanalei River, a
rapid rise was also observed along the South Fork of the Wailua
River. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly,
especially near the Hanalei Bridge on the Kuhio Highway and near
the mouth of the Wailua River. Kuhio Highway remains closed near
the Hanalei Bridge.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
The entire island of Kauai.

killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 31 at 2:24PM HST until October 31 at 4:30PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
SMWHFO

The National Weather Service in Honolulu has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Kauai Leeward Waters...

* Until 430 PM HST.

* At 223 PM HST, a strong capable of producing waterspouts was
located 10 nm southwest of Southern Tip of Niihau, or 39 nm
southwest of Barking Sands, moving east at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Southern Tip of Niihau.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for gusty winds, steep and fast-building seas, and blinding
downpours. Stay low or go below, and make sure all on board are
wearing life jackets.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 31 at 10:46AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds and downstream tidal effects on the St
John River have slowed flow at Astor. Forecast rainfall may lead to
additional rises within Moderate flood stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 3.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM EDT Saturday was 3.7 feet.
- Forecast...Forecast rainfall may lead to additional rises within
Moderate Flood Stage.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1145 PM EDT.
